scope: Source-backed updates to existing API Translation records; each field delta is supported by a maintainer, vendor, or standards-body source. Fields are named after the catalog projects table.

fields.platform: OpenGL ES 2.0–3.2 → Vulkan, desktop OpenGL, Direct3D 9/11, or Metal as supported by the selected backend; platform coverage varies by renderer.

sources.label: ANGLE maintainer README and backend/platform support tables

updates.evidence_note: The upstream README identifies the supported OpenGL ES frontends and graphics backends; target OS/backend combinations differ, so the broad prior platform string should retain that caveat.

fields.subtype: Offline PS5 executable relinker with system-library replacements and Vulkan shader/GPU compatibility; title-specific execution remains unverified until it runs.

updates.evidence_note: The maintainer describes host ELF/PE conversion and replacement PRX libraries; conversion is not itself proof of working runtime compatibility, and the project is not a whole-console emulator.

fields.status: v0.3 (2026-09-11); maintainer reports menus, races, saves, physical/touch controls, and high-50s race performance for Android Asphalt 8 v2.0.0e on Vita; user-supplied APK/OBB required.

sources.label: Maintainer repository: exact source build and current feature claims

updates.evidence_note: The release and README scope this compatibility layer to one Android game build; it is a game-specific port/compatibility project rather than a general Android graphics API translator.

fields.status: Experimental; v0.2.18 was released 2026-10-10. The maintainer reports Bloodborne 1.09 playable through Windows/Linux world areas and bosses; the renderer remains hybrid with PM4/compute work and known GPU hangs/hitches.

updates.evidence_note: The current release is a game-specific PS4-to-PC compatibility runtime with custom code and a hybrid Vulkan/PM4 graphics path, not a reusable console graphics API layer.

fields.summary: Game-specific experimental Bloodborne runtime for Linux that runs the PS4 x86-64 game code on the host, reimplements selected services, and currently renders through shadPS4-derived PM4 processing with Vulkan shader recompilation. Direct GNM-call-to-Vulkan translation is described as future work.

updates.evidence_note: The maintainer distinguishes the current command-processor path from a planned direct GNM-to-Vulkan layer; the current project is a title-specific port/runtime rather than a general API translator.

fields.strategy: Commercial Wine-based Windows compatibility product; graphics backends are selectable components including WineD3D, DXVK, DXMT, and Apple D3DMetal. Native ARM64 Mac support is a Preview path using a custom FEX build for x86/x64 code.

sources.label: CodeWeavers CrossOver Mac graphics backend documentation
CodeWeavers native ARM64 Mac Preview announcement

updates.evidence_note: Separates CrossOver’s Windows API compatibility layer from the graphics translation components it can use; native ARM64 Mac support remains explicitly Preview.

fields.platform: Direct3D 8 → Direct3D 9; Windows proxy DLL, with 32-bit and 64-bit builds. It can be chained with a separate D3D9 backend such as DXVK, but does not itself translate to Vulkan.
fields.status: Active source project; v1.16.0 was released 2026-09-23.

updates.evidence_note: The latest release documents a D3D8-to-D3D9 wrapper; the Vulkan leg in common Linux setups belongs to another layer, typically DXVK.

fields.platform: Direct3D 11/12 → Apple Metal on macOS with Apple Silicon; supplied through Apple Game Porting Toolkit and integrated as an optional CrossOver/Wine graphics backend.
fields.strategy: Proprietary Direct3D 11/12-to-Metal graphics translation component; it is not by itself the Windows API compatibility layer.

sources.label: CodeWeavers D3DMetal announcement and named game examples

updates.evidence_note: The product is proprietary and integrated into a broader Windows compatibility environment; platform and graphics API roles should be separated in the record.

fields.status: Active; latest listed release v0.1.20260608 was published 2026-06-09. Maintainers report many CLI apps work while GUI support is still developing; the Metal backend is an initial implementation powered by Vulkan translation.

sources.label: Darling maintainer README: system architecture and Metal backend maturity

updates.evidence_note: Darling primarily reconstructs macOS system APIs/frameworks on Linux; its experimental Metal backend is a component and should not be presented as the project’s main graphics API translation method.

fields.platform: Direct3D 10/11 → Metal; macOS through Wine/CrossOver, with the project primarily documenting x86-64 Wine DLL builds.
fields.status: Active experimental graphics layer; latest release v0.80 was published 2026-04-23; game-specific fixes and compatibility issues remain documented.

sources.label: DXMT maintainer repository and install guidance

updates.evidence_note: The release history supersedes the prior v0.70 status; supported usage is Wine/CrossOver on macOS and should not be broadened to native Windows applications.

fields.platform: Direct3D 8/9/10/11 → Vulkan; primarily Linux through Wine/Proton, with 32-bit and 64-bit builds. Windows use is explicitly community-supported/unsupported by upstream. The same repository also provides a native library mode for porting without Wine.
fields.status: Active; DXVK 3.1.1 was released 2026-09-15. Current 3.x driver requirements and Wine winevulkan requirements are listed in the maintainer wiki.

sources.label: DXVK upstream README and API coverage

updates.evidence_note: The upstream README now lists D3D8 alongside D3D9–11 and describes DXVK Native; the native path is for application/game ports and does not use Wine.

fields.status: Experimental/stale Mac-specific build line; latest listed release v1.10.3-20230507-repack was published 2024-07-23. The project relies on Wine and MoltenVK for the D3D10/11→Vulkan→Metal path; current compatibility with modern Wine/MoltenVK is not established.

updates.evidence_note: The available release/build line is distinct from upstream DXVK and should not inherit upstream’s current support claims.

fields.summary: A game-specific native PC port/compatibility runtime for inFAMOUS: Second Son. It runs the PS4 x86-64 game code on Windows/Linux hosts, replaces selected PS4 services, and translates GPU work to Vulkan; compatibility claims apply only to the documented game build and tested hardware.

sources.label: Maintainer repository: method and exact game build requirements

updates.evidence_note: This is a title-specific port that includes graphics translation, not a general PS4 API layer; keep that distinction visible in its summary/subtype.

fields.status: Experimental PlayStation 5 emulator; the latest listed release tag is KytyPS5-2026-10-16-83db2ef (published 2026-10-16 UTC). The project reports title-dependent boot/rendering results; its compatibility notes do not establish broad gameplay compatibility.
fields.strategy: Hybrid console emulation with an RDNA2 shader recompiler that translates guest GPU programs to SPIR-V/Vulkan; system and CPU execution are part of the emulator, not a standalone graphics API layer.

sources.label: Maintainer project documentation and emulator description

updates.evidence_note: The repository describes the product as an emulator and names its executable kyty_emulator; reclassifying it avoids treating the Vulkan shader recompiler as the whole project. The release page date is UTC and differs from the New York review date.

fields.status: Alpha; v0.1.0 was published 2026-07-22. The README describes Metal API and shader translation into Vulkan pipelines, with several newer render/compute stages still project scope rather than a general-purpose production compatibility claim.

sources.label: Metal2Vulkan maintainer README and implementation scope

updates.evidence_note: The release page gives a stable version/date and the maintainer docs identify the language/license; keep alpha maturity explicit.

fields.platform: Direct3D 11 user-mode driver/DDI → Direct3D 12; Windows 10 OS component, selected by applications through D3D11On12CreateDevice and requiring a D3D12-capable driver/device.
fields.summary: Microsoft’s D3D11 user-mode driver mapping layer submits D3D11 work to D3D12 and supports interop with D3D12. It is an opt-in Windows component, not a drop-in d3d11.dll replacement; Microsoft says source builds are intended for local testing.

sources.label: Microsoft D3D11On12 README: mapping model, device selection, and usage caveat

updates.evidence_note: The maintainer documentation defines the exact DDI-level mapping and application opt-in, which is more precise than a generic D3D11-to-D3D12 DLL description.

fields.summary: A C++ helper library implementing D3D11-style graphics constructs on Direct3D 12. Microsoft documents it as the shared lower layer used by the Windows D3D11On12 and D3D9On12 components; it is developer integration infrastructure, not a standalone compatibility DLL.
fields.status: Active developer library; Microsoft repository received changes on 2026-10-12.

sources.label: Microsoft D3D12 Translation Layer README and architecture

updates.evidence_note: Clarifies that the project is a library used by the two Windows mapping layers rather than another application-facing translation layer.

fields.platform: Direct3D 9 user-mode driver/DDI → Direct3D 12; Windows 10 OS component, selected through Direct3DCreate9On12 and requiring a D3D12-capable driver/device.
fields.summary: Microsoft’s Direct3D 9 driver mapping layer submits D3D9 commands to D3D12. Applications select the D3D9On12 device through the documented creation API; it is not a replacement d3d9.dll, and source builds are for local testing.

sources.label: Microsoft D3D9On12 README: API selection and mapping caveat

updates.evidence_note: The project README documents DDI mapping and device opt-in, distinguishing this OS component from third-party D3D9 wrapper DLLs.

fields.platform: Vulkan 1.4 subset → Apple Metal; macOS, iOS, tvOS, visionOS, Mac Catalyst, and supported Apple simulators/architectures.
fields.status: Active Khronos open-source layered implementation; latest listed release MoltenVK 1.4.2 was published 2026-07-24. It implements a Vulkan subset over Metal, with feature coverage defined by its current documentation.

sources.label: Khronos MoltenVK README and supported platforms

updates.evidence_note: Adds a dated release and makes clear that MoltenVK is a layered Vulkan implementation over Metal, not an API for running Windows executables by itself.

fields.status: Pre-1.0 research build. The maintainer’s 2026-09-30 PRD says none of the five gate-title requirements had been demonstrated in a gate-title run; most titles are reported not to boot. Windows PC host and user-supplied decrypted PS5 files are required.

sources.label: Maintainer PRD: dated compatibility gate status
Maintainer user guide: requirements and limitations

updates.evidence_note: The project translates/rel links PS5 binaries and APIs toward Windows/Vulkan, but status should remain pre-release and explicitly experimental; a conversion success is not gameplay compatibility.

fields.status: Experimental; latest listed release v0.2.4 was published 2026-10-10. The compatibility tracker counts boot/menu/gameplay milestones separately and explicitly does not claim full-game playability from those stages.

updates.evidence_note: The release status is current, while the compatibility tracker supplies the important limitation that milestones do not establish complete playability.

fields.status: Active; latest listed stable branch release Proton 11.0-2e was published 2026-10-09, alongside the Experimental channel. WineD3D can be selected as an OpenGL backend in place of Vulkan-based DXVK for supported Direct3D versions.

sources.label: Valve Proton README: selectable graphics path

updates.evidence_note: Proton is the full Wine-based Windows compatibility stack; DXVK and WineD3D are graphics components within it, not synonyms for Proton.

fields.summary: A title-specific native PC port/compatibility runtime for The Last Guardian. It runs PS4 x86-64 game code on host Windows/Linux, reimplements selected PS4 services, and translates GPU work to Vulkan; the supported input is the user’s dump of CUSA03627 update 01.03.

sources.label: Maintainer README: exact PS4 dump and method

updates.evidence_note: This entry is a game-specific native port that contains graphics/API translation, rather than a reusable PS4 API layer.

fields.platform: Direct3D 12 → Vulkan; primarily Linux through Wine/Proton, with Windows builds mainly intended for development/testing. Project docs cover x86 32/64-bit and aarch64 cross-builds; usable feature set depends on the Vulkan driver.
fields.status: Active Proton graphics component; latest listed release v3.0.1 was published 2026-05-06.

updates.evidence_note: The release and README clarify the Linux/Wine primary target, Windows development-build caveat, and driver requirements; this is the gaming-focused fork, separate from Wine upstream vkd3d.

fields.platform: Direct3D 12 → Vulkan for Windows applications running through Wine on Unix-like hosts; upstream Wine library, distinct from vkd3d-proton.
fields.status: Active Wine upstream project; WineHQ announced vkd3d 2.1 on 2026-08-24. Release notes define feature coverage; the API is not presented as fully conformant D3D12.

updates.evidence_note: Separates Wine upstream from the Proton-oriented fork and retains feature-level caveats instead of implying complete D3D12 parity.

fields.summary: An Xbox One ERA compatibility layer for Windows UWP that implements selected Xbox system interfaces, including KernelX and D3D11.X, and runs supported title binaries through Windows services. It is a partial API/system compatibility project, not a full Xbox hardware emulator.

sources.label: WinDurango maintainer README: architecture, Windows host requirements, and title status

updates.evidence_note: The README describes API/system-library coverage and title-specific compatibility, so records should not imply general Xbox One emulation or complete title support.

fields.platform: Windows user-mode APIs → POSIX host APIs on Linux, macOS, BSD, and other documented Unix-like systems; graphics translation is supplied by components such as WineD3D, DXVK, and vkd3d rather than Wine’s overall API layer alone.
fields.status: Active; Wine 11.0 is the stable release and Wine 11.17 is the latest development release listed on 2026-10-15.

sources.label: WineHQ project description and platform scope

updates.evidence_note: Keeps the operating-system API compatibility layer distinct from the graphics backends it can host; release versions are checked against WineHQ’s own listing.

fields.platform: DirectDraw and Direct3D 1–11 → OpenGL through Wine’s graphics implementation on POSIX hosts; actual feature support depends on the Wine version and host OpenGL driver.
fields.strategy: Wine’s built-in Direct3D/DirectDraw graphics implementation maps rendering calls to host OpenGL; it is one graphics component in Wine, separate from DXVK and vkd3d.

sources.label: Wine developer archive: WineD3D/OpenGL implementation context
Valve Proton README: WineD3D selectable backend

updates.evidence_note: The record should identify OpenGL as WineD3D’s graphics backend and avoid implying that the WineD3D component covers Wine’s entire Windows API surface.

fields.platform: Desktop OpenGL → Vulkan through Mesa Gallium; requires a usable Vulkan driver, and the exposed OpenGL version/features depend on Mesa and the underlying Vulkan device/driver.
fields.strategy: Mesa Gallium OpenGL frontend implemented by emitting Vulkan calls; driver, not an emulator or operating-system compatibility layer.

sources.label: Mesa Zink driver documentation: implementation and requirements

updates.evidence_note: Makes the API direction explicit and records that Zink depends on a Vulkan-capable host driver, with feature ceilings determined by the underlying device.
